text:
ashok: Heads up — eviction rates in us-west1 spot pools jumped to ~18% over the last 6h. We're seeing oscillation every 20–40s per instance. Need a routing plan to reduce churn impact on Std/Pro customers. Thoughts?

kevin: Ack. Are these the older T4 spot sets or the newer A10g preemptibles?

maria: Mostly a mix. Older T4 spot pools are thrashing; autoscaler is bouncing instances and causing KV cache churn. A10g preemptibles are more stable but still affected.

li: Suggest a short-circuit strategy: keep hotspots sticky for 30–60s per request key and prefer local quantized model_variant before doing cross-region failover. That avoids re-JIT/rehydration hits.

ashok: Proposal sketch: tier-aware routing — Prod customers: prefer dedicated -> quantized local variant -> cross-region fallback. Free tier: best-effort spot only with exponential retry/backoff. Also use aggressive KV reuse when switching.

jen: Can we get a quick cost estimate? If we shift 20% of Std traffic off spot to dedicated what's the monthly $ delta and ops impact?

kevin: Draft config for discussion:
```
route_policies:
  - name: tiered_spot_mitigation
    priority_chain:
      - type: dedicated
      - type: local_variant
        variant: quantized
      - type: spot
        region: us-west1
    sticky_window_sec: 30
    retry_backoff_ms: [50, 200, 1000]
    spot_eviction_threshold: 0.12
    regional_failover_limit_qps: 50
```
I can open a PR with tests.

maria: A couple notes: 1) sticky_window should be per-request-key (user/session/model_key) otherwise cache fragmentation. 2) spot_eviction_threshold 0.12 is too low given current 0.18; set to 0.20 so we trigger failover earlier. 3) add a cooldown per-instance to avoid flip-flop.

opsbot: [alert] us-west1 spot eviction rate 18% over 6h; autoscaler triggered 43 times. Details: https://ops.internal/evictions/176999

ashok: Ok set threshold to 0.20 and sticky_window to 45s. Kevin — add quantized local_variant before cross-region fallback (we want to avoid network latency). Also add circuit-breaker to limit concurrent region failovers.

kevin: Will update the PR. Also propose adding a ‘fallback_reason’ tag on metrics and emitting `route.fallback.count{reason=spot_eviction}` so we can join to support tickets and SLO breaches.

li: +1 on metrics. Also recommend we log `fallback_stack` as a short list (e.g. [local_variant, region_failover]) so postmortems are easier.

jen: Quick cost modelling — shifting 20% Std->dedicated rough calc: ~$45k/mo delta but reduces retries and failed requests which lowers support load. I'll run a more precise sim and post numbers.

maria: Let's canary in us-west2 first with synthetic oscillation traffic. Ops — can you schedule a reproducer run?

opsbot: Canary job scheduled: spot-fallback-canary-2026-03-18-2300Z. Job id: canary-176999-42

ashok: Thanks all. If canary looks good, roll to 25% traffic for 24h, then full roll. Keep an eye on `route.fallback.latency` and `model.variant.swap_rate`.

kevin: I'll open the PR today and add unit tests + canary rollout plan.

maria: One more thing: set a soft quota for cross-region failovers to avoid unexpected egress $ spikes. Maybe 10% of total QPS/day as guardrail.

li: Good call. Also plan a small A/B to compare: quantized-local-first vs region-failover-first for end-to-end p95 latency.

jen: I'll coordinate cost-vs-latency dashboards once we have canary metrics.

ashok: Perfect. Thanks — moving to action items: Kevin PR, Ops schedule reproducer (done), Jen cost sim, Li metrics tags, Maria canary monitor.

opsbot: Action items logged: #176999-pr + #176999-canary.
